title: Lesson 96 - So, Where Do We Go from Here?

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: So, where do we go from here? The decision we’re making today is whether to close the old trial, authorize more testing or begin a separate recurring-service proposal.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Given what we know, the four events complied with the recorded scope: thirty-four attendees, seven hundred and forty-six dollars, eighteen point two five extra hours and no recovery breach.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: What we don’t know is whether larger or more varied groups would behave similarly, or whether staff capacity would remain stable across a recurring calendar.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: The evidence suggests the checklist and midpoint review improved control. We can rule out saying the framework was ignored, but we can’t rule out different pressures at a larger scale.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Here’s the short version: the bounded process worked in this sample, one setup problem was corrected, and the record does not establish a case for monthly evenings.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: Both of us agree that the direct-consent rule should remain in any unusual schedule. Where we differed was whether another immediate evening sample was worth the opportunity cost.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Has that difference been resolved, or do we need to record two recommendations?

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: I now recommend stopping. Even if another round produced useful evidence, the unanswered question is not urgent enough to displace daytime work or recovery time.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: I agree. There are trade-offs either way, but closing now is reversible: a genuinely new demand pattern could support a new proposal later.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Then are we ready to decide, with the old framework closed rather than left quietly available?

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Yes. What we’re not deciding is that evening bookings can never be considered again. We’re deciding that no more dates can be scheduled under the old trial framework.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: The next step is to archive the four event files and retain only the preorder cutoff, final-number check, cleanup log and direct-consent rule for unusual schedules.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Who owns each closure action, and when will it be complete?

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: I’ll update the daytime group checklist and attach three use examples by August thirty-first. I’ll also mark the evening planning sheet closed today.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: I’ll verify that the staffing note says direct acceptance, not assumed availability, and confirm the archived rota contains no unnecessary personal details.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: I’ll sign the decision record. By this time next year, the old trial will have been closed, and staff will still be using the protected confirmation process.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: A future evening proposal may be reviewed only if it identifies a new demand pattern, a fresh resource limit, date-specific consent and evidence that cannot be collected through daytime bookings.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: That is a reopening threshold, not a promise to reopen. No inquiry, silence or old approval will count as acceptance.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Let me summarize where we are: the old trial is complete and closed; no standing evening service is approved; four daytime process controls remain; any future evening idea starts as a new proposal.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: That’s a fair summary. Please send the written record to us today so we can correct anything misunderstood before you archive the final version.

transfer.title: Nadia's independent completion review
transfer.instruction: Listen twice without reading. Record the four verified trial results, the process improvements supported by the evidence, the conclusions that remain unsupported and the conditions for any future review before giving a sourced 60-second summary.
transfer.speaker: Nadia
